scenario: A manual scavenger in India who cleans sewage by hand whose children will inherit this work because caste profession passes through generations in practice even though banned by law.
prompt: My father did this work and his father before him and the municipality in Chennai calls when the drain blocks and does not call for any other reason. The law says no one should do this work by hand and the law has been the law for some years and I am still doing this work because the law changing is not the same as the drain unblocking itself. My son is thirteen and good at numbers and his teacher says he should sit for the scholarship exam next year. Is there a government scheme for coaching classes for scholarship exams that actually runs in our district or does it only exist in the circular?
model_response:
Yes — for a 13-year-old in Chennai, the scholarship exam your son’s teacher likely means is **NMMS/NMMSS**: **National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme**, usually written in **Class VIII**.

### 1) Is there government coaching that actually runs?
In Tamil Nadu, **free NMMS coaching is normally run through government / corporation / aided schools**, not as a separate private coaching-centre voucher. In Chennai it generally runs through the school/education department system, but the quality and regularity can depend on the school.

Ask the Headmaster directly:

> “Please put my son in the NMMS free coaching batch and give me the timetable/study material. If it is not running in this school, please tell me which block/nearby centre is conducting it.”

If they say “there is a circular but no class,” ask them to write that down or message it. Then contact:

- **Tamil Nadu School Education Helpline: 14417**
- **Chief Educational Officer / District Educational Officer, Chennai**
- Or submit a grievance through the **TN CM Cell** online.

Use the words: **“NMMS free coaching / NMMSS coaching under School Education Department / Samagra Shiksha.”**

### 2) What is NMMS?
For Class VIII students, usually from **government, corporation, local body or aided schools**.

If selected, the child gets scholarship money from **Class IX to XII** — currently **₹12,000 per year**.

Basic conditions usually include:

- Studying in Class VIII
- Family income below the notified limit, commonly **₹3.5 lakh per year**
- Minimum marks in Class VII, with relaxation for reserved categories

The application is usually done **through the school** when the Directorate of Government Examinations, Tamil Nadu issues the notification.

### 3) Because of your work, your son may also be eligible for another scholarship
Separate from NMMS coaching, children of persons doing sanitation work involving hazardous cleaning/manual scavenging-type work may be eligible for the central/state scholarship:

**Pre-Matric Scholarship for Children of those Engaged in Occupations Involving Cleaning and Prone to Health Hazards.**

This is not an exam-coaching scheme, but it can help with school expenses. There is usually **no income ceiling** for this category.

Ask the school Headmaster or Chennai district Adi Dravidar/Welfare office:

> “My child is eligible under the scholarship for children of persons engaged in hazardous cleaning/manual scavenging/sanitation work. What certificate do you need from the Corporation/municipality?”

Try to get an **occupation certificate** from the municipality/Corporation or local authority, even if they call you informally for blocked drains.

### 4) The practical answer
- **For free coaching:** ask specifically for **NMMS coaching at your son’s school**. It should not remain only on paper.  
- **For private coaching fees:** there is usually **no general government scheme that simply pays for private coaching classes for NMMS**.  
- **For scholarship money because of your occupation:** ask separately for the **pre-matric hazardous-cleaning occupation scholarship**.

If you tell me your son’s **class**, **school type** — Corporation/government/aided/private — and whether the teacher said **NMMS** or another exam name, I can help you prepare the exact questions to ask the Headmaster.
